question.text: Common purposes that can use currency futures for hedging include:

answer.text: Imports/exports, foreign travel, education and medical payments abroad, foreign-currency loans, overseas investments/repatriation, and INR loan installments for foreign-currency earners
Only loan repayments in foreign currency
Only investment in assets outside India

explanation.text: The Logic: The workbook lists currency futures hedging use cases that include imports and exports, foreign travel, education fees and medical treatment abroad, employee payments abroad, foreign-currency loans, overseas investment and repatriation, and INR loan installments paid by foreign-currency earners. All of these create cross-border currency exposure that can be hedged using exchange-traded currency futures. The Trap: The distractors each restrict hedging to a single use case (only trade transactions, only loan repayments, or only overseas investments). Currency hedging is not limited to one category — any cross-border cash flow that creates currency exposure is a candidate for hedging. Note: Replaced the answer-randomization-fragile 'All of the above' wording with a standalone comprehensive option that lists the supported use cases, and removed the cross-exam/pro-tip lines that were not source-grounded.
